newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian shares surge, Mibtel index ends at record.
newsitem.headline: Italian shares surge, Mibtel index ends at record.

text.p: Italian shares surged on EMU euphoria along with Italian bond futures on Monday with the all-share Mibtel index ending at a new all-time high above 13,800 and the Mib30 blue chip index above 21,020 but just off a historic 21,028 peak.

Dealers said trading took off after a sluggish morning on news European Union finance ministers said Italy was on track to qualify for the single currency in 1999 as long as Italy promised to keep taking necessary steps to make the grade.

The Mibtel index ended 1.44 percent up at 13,804 record high, the Mib30 blue chip index ended 1.49 percent up at 21,025 and the Fib30 Sept stock index future was at a late 21,200 versus a new 21,250 record high.

Technical barriers fell like ninepins on Monday afternoon right up to the close. "It wasn't surprising the Bourse climbed with Italian Btp bond futures solidly above 136.00 and the spread over Bunds in at 100 basis points," one dealer said.
Telecoms stocks showed a strong recovery, with Telecom Italia closing 3.71 percent up at 5,646 lire and Stet holding up 3.82 percent at 10,186.
In firmer banks, Banca Commerciale Italiana gained 4.32 percent to 4,224 lire and Banco Ambrosiano Veneto jumped 6.47 percent to 6,153.
Bellwether stock ENI put on 0.81 percent to 10,050 lire and Olivetti gained 1.76 percent to 491.1 with over 24 million shares changing hands, the leading gainer by volume of the session.
Total traded volume estimated at 1.32 trillion lire, just a touch lower than Friday's 1.34 trillion lire.

Traders noted that despite recent strong rallies, the Italian stock market had a way to go yet before equalling historic highs of May 20, 1986 when the authoritative BCI (Comit) general index reached 908.20. The BCI index, updated once a day after the close, ended on Monday at 858.92.
